title: Saxons
capsule: The Saxons were a Germanic tribal confederation that emerged along the lower Elbe and North Sea coasts by the third century CE, first attested in Roman sources around 286 when they were raiding the shores of Britain and Gaul alongside the Franks. Over the following centuries Saxon groups migrated into Britain, where they gave their name to the kingdoms of Essex, Sussex, and Wessex, while the continental Saxons maintained independence from the Frankish kingdoms until Charlemagne's thirty-year Saxon Wars (772–804) forcibly Christianized and incorporated them into the Carolingian empire. The dataset's to date of 800 reflects the formal subjugation, after which 'Saxons' appears as a Carolingian administrative duchy rather than an independent political entity.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Saxons were a tribal confederation without fixed territorial boundaries, making precise mapping inherently uncertain; their core territory between the Rhine, Elbe, and North Sea is generally agreed upon in modern scholarship.
